minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved a change of use at 43 Summer Street and the SSO notification and CTE year-three contracts.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the engineer for a proposed retail marijuana dispensary at the former Donnelly's Tavern and voted on the change of use. It also approved a Wright-Pierce SSO notification contract and the year-three CTE contract increase, voted to hold the May 31 meeting in person with a Zoom option, and reviewed town meeting results and project updates. The chair announced it was his last meeting as chair.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none was apparent in the captions.
Chair asked for public comment at the end; none was seen online.

votes.motion: Accept the change of use at 43 Summer Street from restaurant to retail.
Roll call on the 43 Summer Street change of use, repeated after Brett Ramsey joined audio; members voted hi.
Accept the SSO notification contract with Wright-Pierce.
Accept the year-three increase to the CTE contract and send the explanatory letter to the procurement officer.
Hold the May 31 meeting in person, amended to allow a Zoom option.
Accept the minutes of the April 12 meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The contract to put an SSO notification plan in place, required by DEP, was described as a small cost and had been approved by counsel.
CTE raised year three due to rising costs, with increases on the O&M portion and on the hourly rate for extra services. The procurement officer wanted a letter for the file.
The betterment was described as a figure in the fifty-something thousand range. Letters will go to residents up to Broad Meadow Drive only, because going further would need a pump station.
The business manager will process an invoice from Fitchburg that matches the commission's own numbers.
A grease trap customer submitted its reports before daily billing would have started.
The engineer estimated current restaurant flow versus the Title 5 estimate for retail use, showing a decrease.

decisions.decision: The business manager will arrange an afternoon pump station tour with the CTE contractor and the new DPW director, open to all members.
The business manager will move the Il Forno permit ahead, subject to confirming with the building department that occupancy and capacity are not changing.
The May 31 meeting will be in person at Town Hall, with a Zoom option.
Next meetings: May 31 at Town Hall, then June 14 at the DPW; the May 24 date was also mentioned for the election.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted on a change of use at 43 Summer Street from restaurant to retail; the first vote was not audible, so a roll call was repeated.
The commission approved the Wright-Pierce contract for an SSO notification plan, which the state environmental agency requires.
The commission approved a year-three increase to the CTE contract and will send a letter explaining it to the procurement officer.
The commission voted to hold its May 31 meeting in person at Town Hall, amended to allow a Zoom option.
The business manager will move the Il Forno permit ahead once the building department confirms occupancy and capacity are not changing.

why_it_matters: The change of use sets how much flow a former restaurant site sends into the sewer system, which ratepayers share.
The CTE year-three increase and the SSO notification contract are sewer operating costs, and they are paid through sewer rates and fees.
watch_next: Next meetings: May 31 at Town Hall with a Zoom option, then June 14 at the DPW.
The pump station tour with the CTE contractor and the new DPW director, to be scheduled by the business manager.
